speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly how your double vision has developed, when it started, and whether it changes if you look up, down, left, or right. Additionally, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, speaking clearly, or weakness in your arms and legs?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pattern of diplopia worsening with upward or downward gaze, combined with fatigable weakness in your limbs that improves with rest, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Given your difficulty climbing stairs and upper limb weakness, I need to confirm the extent of your bulbar involvement and assess reflexes.

REQUEST TEST: Routine Blood Work (CBC, ESR, Creatine Kinase, Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies)
REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve Stimulation

REQUEST IMAGES: EMG_Nerve_Conduction_Study

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies and a decreased muscle response on repetitive nerve stimulation confirms a defect at the neuromuscular junction. Given your specific symptoms of diplopia worsening with upward or downward gaze and fatigable limb weakness, are you currently experiencing drooping of your eyelids (ptosis) or difficulty swallowing?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
